### workspace capture --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace capture [project] [options]

Read a tmux pane's scrollback buffer and print it to stdout.
Defaults to the bottommost pane and last 100 lines.

Options:
        --name WS                    The project, as an option (same as the positional [project])
        --pane N                     Target pane: zero-based index, 'window.pane' (e.g. '0.1', from 'workspace sessions'), a tmux pane id (e.g. '%19', from 'workspace sessions --json'), 'bottom', or a title substring (e.g. 'Claude Code'). A title is matched against the raw pane title, then the agent label shown in 'workspace sessions' TITLE; the first matching pane wins, so use 'window.pane' or a '%id' to be exact
        --lines N                    Number of lines from the bottom to capture (default: 100)
        --all                        Capture full pane history up to tmux history-limit

Examples:
  workspace capture    # last 100 lines of the bottommost pane, project auto-detected
  workspace capture scooter --lines 200    # last 200 lines of an explicit project
  workspace capture --name scooter    # the same project, named with --name
  workspace capture scooter --all    # full pane history
  workspace capture scooter --pane 1    # specific pane by index
  workspace capture scooter | grep ERROR    # composable — pipe to other tools
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace capture
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
Usage: workspace capture [project] [options]

Defaults to the bottommost pane and last 100 lines.

Options:
        --name WS                    The project, as an option (same as the positional [project])
        --pane N                     Target pane: zero-based index, 'window.pane' (e.g. '0.1', from 'workspace sessions'), a tmux pane id (e.g. '%19', from 'workspace sessions --json'), 'bottom', or a title substring (e.g. 'Claude Code'). A title is matched against the raw pane title, then the agent label shown in 'workspace sessions' TITLE; the first matching pane wins, so use 'window.pane' or a '%id' to be exact
        --lines N                    Number of lines from the bottom to capture (default: 100)
        --all                        Capture full pane history up to tmux history-limit

Examples:

  workspace capture scooter --lines 200    # last 200 lines of an explicit project
  workspace capture --name scooter    # the same project, named with --name
